dedupe_keys.name: additional tennessee eastman process simulation data for anomaly detection evaluation

description: The Tennessee Eastman Process is a simulated chemical plant widely used as a benchmark for process control and fault detection. Its coverage is one simulated plant, not a real location. This dataset, referenced in Rieth et al. (2017) and sponsored by the U.S. Office of Naval Research, provides a much larger set of simulation runs than the original benchmark: fault-free and faulty training and testing sets, each run from a different random seed (500 runs, with non-overlapping seeds between training and testing), with faults 1 to 20 introduced one hour into training runs and eight hours into testing runs. Each table has 55 columns: fault number, simulation run, sample index, and 52 process variables sampled every three minutes over 25 hours (training) or 48 hours (testing). The four files are R data frames (.RData), from 24 MB to 837 MB, published on Harvard Dataverse on 6 July 2017. The data are dedicated to the public domain under the provider's user agreement, which disclaims liability. Caveats: it is simulated data from one reference process, and the RData format needs R or a converter. For simulation it is a standard benchmark for fault detection, anomaly detection and digital twin monitoring of chemical plants. Related catalogue records include DWSIM and the NASA Prognostics Data Repository.
